baseVerse.he: כִּי לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה אֲדֹנָי ה' דָּבָר כִּי אִם גָּלָה סוֹדוֹ אֶל עֲבָדָיו הַנְּבִיאִים
baseVerse.en: For the Lord God does nothing without revealing His counsel to His servants the prophets.

secondaryVerse.he: הִכְרַתִּי גוֹיִם נָשַׁמּוּ פִנּוֹתָם הֶחֱרַבְתִּי חוּצוֹתָם מִבְּלִי עוֹבֵר נִצְדּוּ עָרֵיהֶם מִבְּלִי אִישׁ מֵאֵין יוֹשֵׁב. אָמַרְתִּי אַךְ תִּירְאִי אוֹתִי תִּקְחִי מוּסָר
secondaryVerse.en: I have cut off nations, their towers are desolate; I have made their streets waste... I said: Surely you will fear Me, you will accept correction.

eventTypes.label: Fire / Destruction
eventTypes.analysis: Fire in Torah thought represents din (strict judgment) descending into the world. R' Nachman teaches that fire comes where shalom (peace) is lacking, because peace is the vessel that holds all blessing. When we see fire, it is a call to increase peace between people and to sweeten harsh judgments through heartfelt prayer, which is the weapon that can reach the root of all decrees.
eventTypes.analysisHe: אש במחשבת התורה מייצגת דין (משפט קשה) היורד לעולם. רבי נחמן מלמד שאש באה במקום שחסר שלום, כי השלום הוא הכלי שמחזיק את כל הברכה.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 14
breslovSources.desc: Drawing peace into the world — peace is the vessel for all blessing and sweetens harsh judgments

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 2
breslovSources.desc: Prayer is the weapon of Mashiach — through prayer one can sweeten all judgments at their root

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 5
breslovSources.desc: Joy transforms strict judgments (dinim) — through holy joy one can convert judgment to mercy

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 10
breslovSources.desc: The Tzaddik sweetens judgments — how the righteous leader elevates harsh decrees

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 250
breslovSources.desc: Fire of controversy and its rectification through truth

breslovSources.title: Likutay Tefilos 14
breslovSources.desc: Prayer for peace in the world and sweetening of harsh judgments

traditionalSources.desc: Fire of judgment (esh din) descends when the left side is aroused without being included in the right (chesed)
Fire comes to a city only because of desecration of Shabbat
Natural events are instruments of divine providence — destruction is a call to return to the Source

eventTypes.label: Flood / Water Disaster
eventTypes.analysis: The Mabul (Great Flood) came because of theft and immorality. Water represents chesed (kindness) — but chesed without boundaries becomes destructive. R' Nachman teaches that the flood waters represent the overwhelming thoughts and worries that drown the mind, and the Teyva (Ark) — which also means 'word' — is the refuge of holy speech and prayer. When we see flooding, it reminds us that even kindness needs the boundaries of Torah.
eventTypes.analysisHe: המבול בא בגלל גזל ועריות. מים מייצגים חסד — אבל חסד בלי גבולות הופך להרס.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 8
breslovSources.desc: The Teyva (Ark/Word) — entering the words of prayer as Noah entered the Ark, a shelter from the flood of worldly confusion

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 56
breslovSources.desc: The melody of water — how the song of creation flows through all of nature

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 8
breslovSources.desc: The great teaching on faith — every person must cross the narrow bridge of life without fear

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 64
breslovSources.desc: Coming to Pharaoh (the source of chaos) — confronting the deepest places of concealment

breslovSources.title: Likutay Tefilos 8
breslovSources.desc: Prayer to be saved from the floodwaters of confusion and to find the holy words

traditionalSources.desc: The Mabul came through the opening of the "windows of heaven" — when the upper waters of judgment are released without mercy
The generation of the Flood was judged by water because they corrupted their ways upon the earth
This world is like a raging sea — only Torah and mitzvos keep a person afloat

eventTypes.label: War / Military Conflict
eventTypes.analysis: R' Nachman reveals that all wars in the world stem from disputes among Torah scholars, and the root of all conflict is a lack of emunah (faith). True victory is not through physical might but through prayer — the weapon of Mashiach. Every war in the physical world reflects a spiritual battle between holiness and impurity. The path to peace begins with seeking peace in one's own heart and home.
eventTypes.analysisHe: רבי נחמן מגלה שכל המלחמות בעולם נובעות ממחלוקות בין תלמידי חכמים, ושורש כל הסכסוך הוא חוסר אמונה.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 2
breslovSources.desc: Prayer is the weapon of Mashiach — the ultimate victory comes through prayer, not physical warfare

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 14
breslovSources.desc: Drawing peace into the world — raising God's honor to its root brings universal peace

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 75
breslovSources.desc: Wars come from dispute among Torah scholars — the spiritual root of physical conflict

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 44
breslovSources.desc: The importance of praying for peace and for the welfare of the nation

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 1
breslovSources.desc: Tiku Emunah — the blast of faith that shatters all barriers and brings the ultimate redemption

breslovSources.title: Likutay Tefilos 2
breslovSources.desc: Prayer for the power of prayer to overcome all enemies

traditionalSources.desc: When Israel below is fragmented, the nations above are empowered — unity below brings peace above
When the shofar is blown in a city, shall not the people tremble? (Amos 3:6)
Wars and national upheavals serve as instruments of divine judgment and correction

eventTypes.label: Earthquake / Tremor
eventTypes.analysis: When the earth trembles, it reflects that the foundations of the world are shaking. R' Nachman teaches that the foundations of the world rest on truth and faith. When these are weakened — when falsehood and atheism spread — the very ground beneath us becomes unstable. An earthquake is Heaven's call to strengthen our foundations: emunah, tefillah, and Torah.
eventTypes.analysisHe: כשהאדמה רועדת, זה משקף שיסודות העולם רועדים. רבי נחמן מלמד שיסודות העולם עומדים על אמת ואמונה.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 5
breslovSources.desc: The world stands on emunah (faith) — when faith weakens, the very foundations tremble

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 64
breslovSources.desc: Approaching the source of concealment — finding God even in the deepest darkness

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 1
breslovSources.desc: Emunah is the foundation — all of creation is sustained by faith

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 4
breslovSources.desc: The Tzaddik is the foundation of the world (Yesod Olam)

breslovSources.title: Likutay Tefilos II 5
breslovSources.desc: Prayer to strengthen faith when the world feels unstable

traditionalSources.desc: Earthquakes occur when Hashem looks at the world and sees idolatry — He sighs and the earth shakes
The earth trembles when strict judgment is aroused below
Natural disasters serve as wake-up calls for humanity to examine its ways

eventTypes.label: Economic Crisis / Financial
eventTypes.analysis: R' Nachman teaches that livelihood (parnasa) comes from emunah (faith). When a person has complete faith, their sustenance flows easily. Economic crises remind us that true wealth is not in markets but in our connection to Hashem. The way to sweeten financial difficulty is through charity (tzedakah), which opens the channels of blessing, and through hitbodedut (personal prayer), speaking to Hashem about our needs with simple trust.
eventTypes.analysisHe: רבי נחמן מלמד שפרנסה באה מאמונה. כשלאדם יש אמונה שלמה, פרנסתו זורמת בקלות.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 7
breslovSources.desc: Livelihood depends on da'at (holy knowledge) — the more connected to Hashem, the easier sustenance flows

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 13
breslovSources.desc: Charity opens the gates of sustenance — giving tzedakah is the key to receiving blessing

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 23
breslovSources.desc: Through joy one draws down abundance — sadness constricts the channels of blessing

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 69
breslovSources.desc: Desire for money pulls a person away from holiness — the rectification of financial desire

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 1
breslovSources.desc: Everything depends on emunah — faith sustains even through financial hardship

breslovSources.title: Likutay Tefilos II 7
breslovSources.desc: Prayer for honest livelihood and freedom from financial worry

traditionalSources.desc: Blessing is found only in things hidden from the eye — true sustenance comes through trust in Hashem
The world's sustenance flows through the mazal (spiritual pipeline) — tzedakah opens it
Trust in Hashem (bitachon) is the foundation of receiving sustenance

eventTypes.label: Disease / Pandemic
eventTypes.analysis: R' Nachman teaches that all illness originates from a lack of joy. Sadness weakens the body and spirit, while simcha (joy) is the greatest medicine. Plagues come to awaken teshuvah (repentance) and to remind us of our mortality so that we use each day wisely. The ultimate healer is Hashem, and the Tzaddik who can reach the root of suffering can bring healing to the entire generation.
eventTypes.analysisHe: רבי נחמן מלמד שכל מחלה נובעת מחוסר שמחה. עצבות מחלישה את הגוף והנפש, בעוד שמחה היא הרפואה הגדולה ביותר.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 24
breslovSources.desc: It is a great mitzvah to be joyful always — joy is the foundation of health and spiritual life

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 14
breslovSources.desc: Peace and healing are connected — where there is peace, there is wholeness (shleimut)

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 3
breslovSources.desc: Finding the good points — searching for merit even in times of suffering brings spiritual healing

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 31
breslovSources.desc: The song of healing — the ten kinds of melody contain the power to heal body and soul

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 277
breslovSources.desc: Medicine and healing — understanding the spiritual roots of physical remedies

breslovSources.title: Sipurey Maasiyos - The Cripple
breslovSources.desc: The story teaches about the connection between joy, music, and healing
breslovSources.snippet: A tale. Once there was a sage. Before his death he called his children and family and left them a will: that they should water trees. "You may engage in other occupations as well, but this you must constantly do: water trees". Afterwards the sage passed away and he left children. And he had one son ...

traditionalSources.desc: If suffering comes upon a person, let them examine their deeds — illness prompts self-reflection
All healing comes from the supernal Tree of Life — connecting to Torah is the root of all cures
Suffering purifies the soul and draws a person closer to their purpose

eventTypes.label: Political Upheaval
eventTypes.analysis: R' Nachman teaches that 'there is no king without a people' — all leadership and authority ultimately derives from Hashem's sovereignty. Political upheaval reflects the reshuffling of divine providence (hashgacha). The rise and fall of leaders is orchestrated from Above to move the world toward its rectification. Our role is to pray for righteous leadership and to strengthen our own inner sovereignty — mastery over our desires.
eventTypes.analysisHe: רבי נחמן מלמד ש'אין מלך בלא עם' — כל מנהיגות וסמכות נובעת בסופו של דבר ממלכות ה'.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 56
breslovSources.desc: The concept of Malkhut (sovereignty) — understanding leadership, authority, and the songs of creation

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 77
breslovSources.desc: Hashem will be King over all the earth — revealing divine sovereignty through Torah and prayer

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 6
breslovSources.desc: Repentance and honor — how teshuvah restores fallen honor and rectifies leadership

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 14
breslovSources.desc: Raising God's honor to its root — the connection between true honor and peace

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 7
breslovSources.desc: Honor and knowledge — when leaders lack true knowledge, governance falters

traditionalSources.desc: The heart of kings and rulers is in the hand of Hashem
All kingdoms receive their power from the Supernal Kingdom — when it shifts, kingdoms below shift
The rise and fall of nations serves the ultimate purpose of revealing divine truth

eventTypes.label: Death of Leader / Public Figure
eventTypes.analysis: R' Nachman teaches that when a Tzaddik or great leader passes from the world, it creates a spiritual void that the generation must fill through increased Torah, prayer, and good deeds. The passing of a notable figure is a wake-up call for the entire generation — reminding us that life is finite and every day must count. At the same time, the righteous continue to influence the world from the Next World even more powerfully than in this one.
eventTypes.analysisHe: רבי נחמן מלמד שכשצדיק או מנהיג גדול נפטר מהעולם, זה יוצר חלל רוחני שהדור צריך למלא.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 4
breslovSources.desc: The Tzaddik is the foundation of the world — the righteous leader sustains and elevates the entire generation

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 61
breslovSources.desc: The power of the Tzaddik's teachings endures beyond physical death

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 66
breslovSources.desc: Understanding death and the eternal nature of the soul

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 8
breslovSources.desc: The world is a narrow bridge — do not fear death, for the soul lives on eternally

breslovSources.title: Sichos HaRan 225
breslovSources.desc: R' Nachman's teachings about the soul's journey after death
breslovSources.snippet: Kabbalah Begins Where Philosophy Ends — There Is No Limit to Its Heights When Rabbainu, o.b.m., was in Uman, someone asked him if it is possible to know the wisdom of Kabbalah without fasts and ritual immersions — for someone had said it is impossible to know Kabbalah except through those means. He ...

traditionalSources.desc: The death of the righteous atones like the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash
The Tzaddik after passing ascends to a higher level and continues to advocate for the generation
The soul continues its journey and growth in the World to Come

eventTypes.label: Terrorist Attack / Violence
eventTypes.analysis: When innocent blood is shed, the Torah demands that we do not become numb or accept it as normal. R' Nachman teaches that the deepest suffering comes from a world where God's light is most concealed. Even in the darkest tragedy, the Torah perspective insists: there is a God who sees, who cares, and who will bring ultimate justice. Our response must be to increase in light — more prayer, more kindness, more Torah — to push back the darkness.
eventTypes.analysisHe: כאשר דם נקי נשפך, התורה דורשת שלא נהיה אדישים. רבי נחמן מלמד שהסבל העמוק ביותר בא מעולם שבו אור ה' מוסתר ביותר.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 64
breslovSources.desc: Come to Pharaoh — finding God even in the deepest concealment and darkest evil

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 8
breslovSources.desc: The world is a narrow bridge — do not be afraid; fear is the real enemy

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 1
breslovSources.desc: Faith pierces through all darkness — emunah is the light that no evil can extinguish

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 5
breslovSources.desc: Joy transforms harsh judgment — even in suffering, finding the spark of holiness

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 12
breslovSources.desc: There are those who go through the greatest darkness yet emerge into the greatest light

breslovSources.title: Likutay Tefilos II 1
breslovSources.desc: Prayer for faith and strength when facing terror and tragedy

traditionalSources.desc: Whoever destroys a single soul, it is as if they destroyed an entire world
Even in the deepest exile and suffering, the Shechinah (Divine Presence) is with Israel
The suffering of the righteous and innocent will ultimately be revealed as purposeful in the World to Come

eventTypes.label: Natural Disaster (General)
eventTypes.analysis: R' Nachman teaches that nature is not separate from Hashem — it is the garment through which divine providence operates. When nature turns destructive, it is a message from the Creator calling His children to wake up and return. The Hebrew word for nature (hateva) has the same letters as 'drowned' (nitba), hinting that within the natural world, holiness is submerged and waiting to be revealed through our prayers and mitzvos.
eventTypes.analysisHe: רבי נחמן מלמד שהטבע אינו נפרד מה' — הוא הלבוש שדרכו פועלת ההשגחה האלוקית.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 52
breslovSources.desc: Gratitude and praise to Hashem in all circumstances — recognizing providence even in calamity

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 5
breslovSources.desc: Emunah — faith that everything Hashem does is for the good, even what we cannot understand

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 56
breslovSources.desc: Each blade of grass sings its song — nature itself contains divine praise and purpose

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 5
breslovSources.desc: Sweetening harsh judgments through joy — transforming gevurah (strictness) into chesed (kindness)

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 8
breslovSources.desc: The whole world is a narrow bridge — courage and faith in times of danger

traditionalSources.desc: Calamities come to the world only on account of Israel — to inspire their return to Hashem
All creation responds to the spiritual state of humanity — nature reflects the soul of the world
Nothing in the physical world happens by chance — every event serves a divine purpose

eventTypes.label: Famine / Hunger / Drought
eventTypes.analysis: The Torah reveals that famine is not merely a physical phenomenon but reflects a spiritual hunger. The prophet Amos warned of a time when there would be a famine 'not of bread, nor thirst for water, but of hearing the words of Hashem.' R' Nachman teaches that physical hunger parallels the soul's hunger for connection to its Creator. The remedy is Torah study and prayer, which nourish both body and soul.
eventTypes.analysisHe: התורה מגלה שרעב אינו רק תופעה פיזית אלא משקף רעב רוחני.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 47
breslovSources.desc: Nourishment of body and soul — the connection between physical eating and spiritual elevation

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 62
breslovSources.desc: Crying out to Hashem in times of need — prayers for sustenance and provision

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 7
breslovSources.desc: Livelihood and sustenance — understanding the spiritual channels of provision

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 13
breslovSources.desc: Tzedakah (charity) sweetens harsh decrees and draws down blessing

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 17
breslovSources.desc: Eating in holiness elevates the sparks of creation

traditionalSources.desc: When there is famine in the city, a person should not eat to excess — solidarity with those who suffer
Famine comes when the higher spiritual channels of abundance are blocked
Physical lack reflects spiritual disconnection — the cure is reconnection

eventTypes.label: Scandal / Corruption
eventTypes.analysis: R' Nachman teaches that truth is the seal of the Holy One — and falsehood cannot endure forever. When scandals are revealed, it is Hashem's light breaking through the darkness of concealment. The exposure of corruption is itself a form of rectification (tikkun). Our response should be to strengthen our own commitment to truth (emes) in speech, business, and relationships.
eventTypes.analysisHe: רבי נחמן מלמד שאמת היא חותמו של הקב"ה — ושקר לא יכול להתקיים לנצח.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 51
breslovSources.desc: Truth and falsehood — the power of truth to overcome all deception

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 64
breslovSources.desc: Faith, truth, and repentance — the spiritual roots of honesty and integrity

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 6
breslovSources.desc: Teshuvah restores what sin has corrupted — repentance is available to everyone

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 10
breslovSources.desc: True judgment and humility — how justice must be administered with mercy

breslovSources.title: Sefer HaMidos - Truth
breslovSources.desc: R' Nachman's collected teachings on the attribute of truth
breslovSources.snippet: One who wants to attach himself to the Blessed G-d, to the extent that he can traverse with his thoughts from Haichal to Haichal (chamber to chamber), and to see the haichaloas (chambers) with the eyes of the intellect, must guard himself from saying falsehood, even by mistake.

traditionalSources.desc: Truth stands on its own (emes has two feet), falsehood cannot stand (sheker has only points)
Truth is the foundation of the world — when truth is compromised, the world itself is endangered
The trait of cleanliness (nekiyut) — maintaining integrity in all dealings

eventTypes.label: Discovery / Scientific Breakthrough
eventTypes.analysis: R' Nachman teaches that every piece of wisdom and every discovery in the world contains a spark of divine wisdom waiting to be elevated. True chochmah (wisdom) recognizes that all knowledge ultimately points back to the Creator. Scientific breakthroughs remind us of the infinite depth of Creation and the divine intelligence embedded in every atom. The task is to use new knowledge to serve Hashem and benefit humanity.
eventTypes.analysisHe: רבי נחמן מלמד שכל חכמה וכל גילוי בעולם מכיל ניצוץ של חכמה אלוקית שמחכה להתעלות.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 1
breslovSources.desc: Contemplating the intellect in all things — finding divine wisdom in every aspect of creation

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 64
breslovSources.desc: The depths of wisdom and understanding — seeking truth beyond surface appearances

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 4
breslovSources.desc: Holy knowledge (da'at) — the highest form of wisdom that connects all understanding to its Source

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 12
breslovSources.desc: The greatest wisdom is to not be wise at all — true humility before the infinite Creator

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 24
breslovSources.desc: The unification of all wisdoms under Torah — every science reflects a facet of divine wisdom

traditionalSources.desc: There are three partners in the creation of a person — science reveals the wisdom of the Creator
All wisdoms of the world have roots in the supernal wisdom — Torah is the blueprint of creation
The purpose of creation is for Hashem to bestow goodness — every discovery reveals more of this goodness

eventTypes.label: Miracle / Rescue / Survival
eventTypes.analysis: R' Nachman teaches that miracles are happening constantly — the problem is that we are too asleep to notice them. When an obvious miracle or rescue occurs, it opens our eyes to see Hashem's hand in everything. Recognizing miracles strengthens emunah and brings more miracles. Our response should be praise, thanksgiving, and sharing the story to inspire others — for publicizing miracles (pirsumei nisa) draws down more divine light.
eventTypes.analysisHe: רבי נחמן מלמד שניסים קורים כל הזמן — הבעיה היא שאנחנו ישנים מכדי לשים לב.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 7
breslovSources.desc: Seeing Hashem's hand in everything — recognizing divine providence in daily life

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 5
breslovSources.desc: Emunah reveals miracles — the stronger our faith, the more we see Hashem's wonders

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 1
breslovSources.desc: Faith is the foundation of all miracles — through emunah, the impossible becomes possible

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 2
breslovSources.desc: Prayer draws miracles — the weapon of Mashiach that can overturn all natural limitations

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 52
breslovSources.desc: Gratitude and praise — how thanking Hashem for past miracles draws future ones

traditionalSources.desc: One who experiences a miracle does not recognize it — we must train ourselves to see divine intervention
When Israel praises Hashem for miracles, it opens the gates of heaven for more salvation
Miracles and nature are both expressions of divine will — they differ only in frequency, not in source

eventTypes.label: Peace Treaty / Reconciliation
eventTypes.analysis: Peace (shalom) is the vessel that contains all blessing. R' Nachman teaches that true peace is not merely the absence of conflict but the integration of opposites into a higher unity. Every peace in this world reflects the supernal peace — the unification of Hashem's Name. When we see peace taking root between nations, it is a glimpse of the ultimate peace of the Messianic era.
eventTypes.analysisHe: שלום הוא הכלי שמחזיק את כל הברכה. רבי נחמן מלמד ששלום אמיתי אינו רק היעדר סכסוך אלא שילוב של הפכים לאחדות גבוהה יותר.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 14
breslovSources.desc: Peace is the vessel for all blessing — how to draw peace into the world through Torah

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 80
breslovSources.desc: Making peace between people — the great merit of those who pursue reconciliation

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 27
breslovSources.desc: Ahavat Yisrael (love of fellow Jews) — the foundation upon which peace is built

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 1
breslovSources.desc: The ultimate peace will come through faith — emunah unifies all hearts

breslovSources.title: Likutay Tefilos 14
breslovSources.desc: R' Nosson's prayer for universal peace

traditionalSources.desc: Hashem found no vessel that can contain blessing except peace
Shalom is the Name of Hashem — every act of peace reveals the divine
The pursuit of peace (rodef shalom) is among the highest spiritual attainments

eventTypes.label: Building / Construction
eventTypes.analysis: Every act of building in this world reflects the building of the spiritual Beis HaMikdash (Holy Temple). R' Nachman teaches that the true 'building' is the construction of the soul through Torah, prayer, and good deeds. Physical construction should inspire us to ask: What am I building in my spiritual life? What legacy am I constructing for eternity?
eventTypes.analysisHe: כל מעשה בנייה בעולם הזה משקף את בניית בית המקדש הרוחני.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 2
breslovSources.desc: The spiritual Temple built through prayer — each prayer is a stone in the eternal edifice

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 20
breslovSources.desc: Tikkun HaKlali — the general rectification that repairs all spiritual structures

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 61
breslovSources.desc: Building the world through truth — construction that endures must be founded on honesty

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 7
breslovSources.desc: Creating vessels for divine light — the spiritual architecture of the soul

traditionalSources.desc: A Torah scholar is called a "builder" — one who builds the world through wisdom
The building of the Mishkan (Tabernacle) mirrors the creation of the world
The purpose of creation is to build a dwelling place for divine presence in the lower worlds

eventTypes.label: Education / Schools / Children
eventTypes.analysis: R' Nachman teaches that the breath of children studying Torah is what sustains the entire world. Education is not merely the transmission of information but the kindling of a flame — inspiring the next generation to connect with their Creator. Every child carries a unique purpose, and the role of education is to help each soul discover and fulfill its mission.
eventTypes.analysisHe: רבי נחמן מלמד שהבל פיהם של תינוקות של בית רבן הוא שמקיים את כל העולם.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 1
breslovSources.desc: Torah is the source of all wisdom — learning Torah in order to teach is the highest form of study

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 282
breslovSources.desc: The simplicity of pure prayer — teaching children to speak to Hashem naturally

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 7

breslovSources.title: Sichos HaRan 29
breslovSources.desc: R' Nachman on the importance of raising children with love and patience
breslovSources.snippet: Even if he is held back so that he did not have time, he should study at least one section of the Shulchan Aruch — no matter which one — even if it is not in the place he is holding during his usual order of studies. For a Jew must learn at least some law in the Shulchan Aruch every single day, all ...

traditionalSources.desc: The world is sustained only by the breath of schoolchildren studying Torah
Children's prayers ascend higher than any other — their pure souls have direct access
Each soul descends with a unique mission — education must help reveal it

eventTypes.label: Marriage / Family / Birth
eventTypes.analysis: R' Nachman teaches that every marriage reflects the cosmic union between the Holy One and the Shechinah. Building a Jewish home is the greatest act of creation a person can do — for every child born is a new world. Marriage requires siyata d'Shmaya (divine assistance), and the key to shalom bayit (domestic peace) is humility, patience, and constant prayer.
eventTypes.analysisHe: רבי נחמן מלמד שכל נישואין משקפים את הייחוד העליון בין הקב"ה לשכינה.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 6
breslovSources.desc: Marriage and holiness — the deep connection between teshuvah and building a holy home

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 14
breslovSources.desc: Shalom — peace in the home is the vessel for all blessings

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 56

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 8

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 23
breslovSources.desc: Joy draws down spiritual abundance into the home

traditionalSources.desc: When husband and wife merit, the Shechinah dwells between them
Every soul has a destined partner — marriage is the reunion of two halves
Holiness in the home draws divine presence into the physical world

eventTypes.label: Poverty / Homelessness
eventTypes.analysis: R' Nachman reveals that poverty can be a spiritual test but also a gateway to closeness with Hashem. The Torah commands us to open our hands wide to the poor. Charity (tzedakah) is not merely helping others — it is a tikkun (repair) for the world and for one's own soul. Every person who gives, even a little, becomes a partner with Hashem in sustaining creation.
eventTypes.analysisHe: רבי נחמן מגלה שעוני יכול להיות מבחן רוחני אבל גם שער לקרבת ה'.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 13
breslovSources.desc: The immense power of tzedakah — charity opens all gates and sweetens all judgments

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 4
breslovSources.desc: Hisbodedus (personal prayer) — even the poorest person can speak to Hashem

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 7
breslovSources.desc: Livelihood flows from da'at — knowledge of Hashem is the root of sustenance

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 3
breslovSources.desc: Finding good points even in the depths of poverty and hardship

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 24
breslovSources.desc: Simcha (joy) even in poverty — joy itself is a form of wealth

traditionalSources.desc: Tzedakah is equal to all mitzvot combined — it saves from death and elevates the giver
The poor person who cries out awakens mercy from the highest levels
Compassion and chesed (kindness) are the pillars of divine service

eventTypes.label: Technology / AI / Automation
eventTypes.analysis: R' Nachman teaches that every generation has its unique tests and tools. Technology, like all of creation, is neutral — it can be used for holiness or for its opposite. The Torah perspective sees AI and technology as reflections of the divine attribute of chochmah (wisdom) given to humanity. The key question is: Are we using these tools to come closer to Hashem, or are they pulling us further away?
eventTypes.analysisHe: רבי נחמן מלמד שלכל דור יש את המבחנים והכלים הייחודיים שלו. טכנולוגיה, כמו כל הבריאה, היא ניטרלית.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 1
breslovSources.desc: Finding divine wisdom in all things — even in human creations, there is a spark of the Creator

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 54

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 64

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 5
breslovSources.desc: Faith above intellect — emunah must guide how we use knowledge and technology

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 12
breslovSources.desc: Not being wise in one's own eyes — humility in the face of human achievement

traditionalSources.desc: Whoever knows how to calculate seasons and constellations and fails to do so — the Torah expects us to use knowledge wisely
In the end of days, the wellsprings of wisdom will be opened — a prediction of information age
Humanity was created to master the physical world and elevate it to serve the divine

eventTypes.label: Environmental / Climate
eventTypes.analysis: The Torah begins with creation and entrusts humanity as guardians of the earth. R' Nachman reveals that every blade of grass has a unique song and purpose. Environmental degradation reflects a disconnection from the awareness that the world belongs to Hashem. The remedy is to restore our role as stewards — appreciating nature as a divine gift, not as a resource to exploit.
eventTypes.analysisHe: התורה מתחילה עם הבריאה ומפקידה את האנושות כשומרי הארץ.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 56
breslovSources.desc: Every blade of grass sings a song — the melody of creation and the sanctity of nature

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 11
breslovSources.desc: Hisbodedus in nature — going out to the fields and forests to connect with Hashem through creation

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 1

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 52
breslovSources.desc: Gratitude for creation — praising Hashem for the world He made

traditionalSources.desc: Bal tashchit — the prohibition against needless destruction applies to all of creation
The earth has a soul — mistreating it has spiritual consequences
The physical world is meant to be elevated, not destroyed — stewardship is a divine mandate

eventTypes.label: Antisemitism / Persecution
eventTypes.analysis: R' Nachman teaches that antisemitism is a spiritual phenomenon rooted in the nations' unconscious resistance to the light of Torah that Israel carries. The hatred intensifies when the world most needs the spiritual light that only Israel can provide. Our response is not to despair but to strengthen our identity, increase in Torah and mitzvos, and trust that Hashem protects His people — for 'the Eternal One of Israel does not lie.'
eventTypes.analysisHe: רבי נחמן מלמד שאנטישמיות היא תופעה רוחנית השורשית בהתנגדות האומות לאור התורה שישראל נושא.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 1
breslovSources.desc: Emunah — strengthening faith when persecution arises; faith is the light that darkness cannot overcome

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 64
breslovSources.desc: Coming to Pharaoh — confronting the source of evil and finding Hashem even there

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 8
breslovSources.desc: The world is a narrow bridge — not to be afraid even when surrounded by enemies

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 33
breslovSources.desc: Am Yisrael and the Torah — the eternal bond between the Jewish people and their mission

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 5
breslovSources.desc: Joy in the face of adversity — transforming fear and suffering into spiritual elevation

traditionalSources.desc: Sinai — from there descended hatred (sinah) to the nations, because Israel received the Torah
In every generation, Amalek arises — but Hashem is at war with Amalek for all generations
Israel's suffering serves to purify and elevate the world toward its ultimate rectification

eventTypes.label: Unity / Gathering / Community
eventTypes.analysis: R' Nachman teaches that the ultimate purpose of creation is unity — 'that they may all be one.' When people gather in love and common purpose, they create a vessel for the Shechinah (Divine Presence). Gathering to the Tzaddik (hitkarevut) is one of the highest forms of this unity. Every act of communal gathering reflects the future ingathering of exiles and the unity of all souls.
eventTypes.analysisHe: רבי נחמן מלמד שהתכלית הסופית של הבריאה היא אחדות.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 34
breslovSources.desc: The power of gathering — when Jews come together, the Shechinah rests among them

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 27
breslovSources.desc: Love of fellow Jews — the foundation of true community and the vessel for divine light

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 14
breslovSources.desc: Peace and unity — drawing peace into the world through communal Torah and prayer

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 56
breslovSources.desc: The song of the future — a melody that unites all voices into one harmonious song

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 1
breslovSources.desc: Emunah unites all hearts — faith is the common ground of all souls

traditionalSources.desc: Whenever ten Jews pray together, the Shechinah is with them
Unity below awakens unity Above — bringing the Holy One and the Shechinah together
Love and unity among Israel is the ultimate spiritual achievement

eventTypes.label: Space / Astronomy
eventTypes.analysis: The heavens declare the glory of God. R' Nachman teaches that when we look at the vastness of the cosmos, we should be filled with awe at the greatness of the Creator. Every star, every galaxy, was created with a purpose. The vastness of space humbles us and reminds us that human understanding is infinitely small compared to Hashem's wisdom. Space exploration is humanity gazing toward heaven — may that gaze lead to genuine recognition of the Creator.
eventTypes.analysisHe: השמים מספרים כבוד א-ל. רבי נחמן מלמד שכשמסתכלים על מרחבי היקום, צריכים להתמלא ביראת הכבוד מגדולת הבורא.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 1
breslovSources.desc: Contemplating the divine intellect in all of creation — from the smallest atom to the greatest galaxy

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 5
breslovSources.desc: The fear of Hashem through contemplating His greatness — awe before the infinite Creator

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 12
breslovSources.desc: The greatest wisdom is to know that we know nothing — humility before the vastness of creation

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 56
breslovSources.desc: The song of creation — every element of the cosmos sings its unique melody

traditionalSources.desc: The soul fills the body as Hashem fills the world — as Above, so below
With ten utterances the world was created — the cosmos is sustained by divine speech
The physical universe, in all its vastness, is a garment for spiritual reality

eventTypes.label: Justice / Court / Law
eventTypes.analysis: R' Nachman teaches that true justice flows from the Torah, which is the blueprint of all morality and law. Human courts are meant to reflect the Heavenly Court (Beis Din Shel Ma'alah). When we see justice pursued or perverted in the world, it is a reminder that there is an ultimate Judge who sees all and judges with perfect truth. The highest form of justice is when judgment is tempered with mercy.
eventTypes.analysisHe: רבי נחמן מלמד שצדק אמיתי נובע מהתורה, שהיא תכנית האב של כל המוסר והחוק.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 14

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 3
breslovSources.desc: Judging others favorably — finding the good point even in those who seem guilty

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 51
breslovSources.desc: Truth and justice — the inseparable connection between honesty and righteous judgment

traditionalSources.desc: A judge who renders a truthful verdict becomes a partner with Hashem in creation
The supernal court judges with perfect balance of justice and mercy
Divine judgment operates on principles that transcend human understanding

eventTypes.label: Immigration / Exile / Refugees
eventTypes.analysis: The Jewish people know exile more intimately than any nation. R' Nachman teaches that exile (galut) is not just physical displacement but a spiritual condition — the Shechinah itself is in exile. When we see refugees and displaced people, we should feel the pain of the universal exile and pray for the ultimate redemption. Every person seeking a home reflects the soul seeking its true Home with Hashem.
eventTypes.analysisHe: העם היהודי מכיר את הגלות יותר מכל עם. רבי נחמן מלמד שגלות אינה רק עקירה פיזית אלא מצב רוחני.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 64
breslovSources.desc: The deepest exile — finding Hashem even in the most foreign and dark places

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 8

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 21

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 1

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 13
breslovSources.desc: Charity for the displaced — the merit of helping those in need

traditionalSources.desc: Everywhere Israel was exiled, the Shechinah was exiled with them
The final redemption will gather all exiles — physical and spiritual — back to their Source
Exile serves to scatter sparks of holiness throughout the world for eventual gathering

eventTypes.label: Medical Breakthrough / Healing
eventTypes.analysis: R' Nachman, whose teachings on healing are among the most profound in Jewish thought, reveals that the soul and body are deeply interconnected. Every medical breakthrough is a revelation of divine mercy. The Torah permits doctors to heal, but reminds us that the ultimate Healer is Hashem. Our response to medical breakthroughs should be gratitude — and the recognition that spiritual healing (through teshuvah, tefillah, and simcha) goes even deeper.
eventTypes.analysisHe: רבי נחמן, שתורותיו על ריפוי הן מהעמוקות ביותר במחשבה היהודית, מגלה שהנשמה והגוף קשורים עמוקות.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 24

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 3
breslovSources.desc: Finding the good points — hope and positivity as pathways to recovery

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 14
breslovSources.desc: Peace and wholeness — shalom is the root of all healing

traditionalSources.desc: The Torah gives permission to heal — doctors are agents of divine healing
Every cure in the lower world has a corresponding spiritual root in the upper world
Physical healing reflects spiritual healing — the body and soul heal together

eventTypes.label: Religious Awakening / Teshuvah
eventTypes.analysis: R' Nachman teaches that no one is ever too far to return. Teshuvah (return to Hashem) is the most powerful force in creation — it can transform darkness into light and sins into merits. When we witness spiritual awakenings, it is a sign that the light of Mashiach is drawing nearer. Every soul that returns sends ripples of holiness through the entire universe.
eventTypes.analysisHe: רבי נחמן מלמד שאף אחד אינו רחוק מכדי לחזור. תשובה היא הכוח החזק ביותר בבריאה.

breslovSources.desc: Teshuvah — the great teaching on repentance and its power to rectify everything

breslovSources.desc: There is no despair at all — the foundational principle that return is always possible

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 1

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 4

breslovSources.desc: Restoring the soul — encouragement for those beginning the journey of return
breslovSources.snippet: Through searching and seeking until one finds within oneself some good points — in order to revive oneself and strengthen oneself in His service, may He be blessed — through this, all the tikunim [rectifications] that were accomplished by the Kohanim [Priests] in their Temple service, and the Levi'i...

traditionalSources.desc: Through teshuvah from love, intentional sins are transformed into merits
The power of teshuvah reaches higher than the Torah itself — it preceded creation
Watchfulness (zehirut) is the first step of the soul's return journey

eventTypes.label: Financial Prosperity / Wealth
eventTypes.analysis: R' Nachman teaches that wealth is a test no less challenging than poverty. The purpose of financial blessing is to use it for Torah, chesed (kindness), and tzedakah (charity). True prosperity is not measured by bank accounts but by closeness to Hashem. When we see economic growth, we should ask: Is this wealth being used to reveal God's glory, or to hide it? The wisest person is one who is rich but uses wealth as if poor — with humility and generosity.
eventTypes.analysisHe: רבי נחמן מלמד שעושר הוא מבחן לא פחות מאתגר מעוני.

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 7
breslovSources.desc: Livelihood and knowledge — true prosperity flows from connection to Hashem

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 69
breslovSources.desc: The test of wealth — overcoming the desire for money that pulls one away from holiness

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 13
breslovSources.desc: Tzedakah — using wealth for charity is the key to sustained blessing

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 23
breslovSources.desc: Joy and abundance — holy joy draws down spiritual and physical prosperity

breslovSources.title: Sichos HaRan 51
breslovSources.desc: R' Nachman on the proper attitude toward money and material possessions
breslovSources.snippet: I say that you must certainly seek greatness. Investigate and seek out only the greatest Tzadik.

traditionalSources.desc: Who is rich? One who is happy with their lot — true wealth is inner contentment
Wealth given from Above carries a test — to see if it will be used for holiness
All worldly pleasures are only tests — the soul's true enjoyment is closeness to Hashem

eventTypes.label: Storm / Wind / Hurricane
eventTypes.analysis: Storms in Torah thought represent the ruach (spirit/wind) of divine power moving through the world. R' Nachman teaches that the winds of the world correspond to the breaths of Torah and prayer. When storms rage, they remind us of the awesome power of the Creator and our smallness before Him. The appropriate response is the blessing on thunder and lightning — recognizing that Hashem's power fills the entire world.
eventTypes.analysisHe: סערות במחשבת התורה מייצגות את רוח הכוח האלוקי הנעה בעולם.

breslovSources.desc: The melodies of nature — wind and storms have their own divine song

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 5
breslovSources.desc: Emunah in the storm — maintaining faith when the world feels chaotic and frightening

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan II 8
breslovSources.desc: The narrow bridge — courage in the face of overwhelming natural forces

breslovSources.title: Likutay Moharan 5
breslovSources.desc: Sweetening harsh judgments — how joy and prayer can calm the storms of judgment

traditionalSources.desc: On thunder, say: Blessed is He whose power fills the world. On lightning: who performs the work of creation
The four winds correspond to the four letters of Hashem's Name — storms are divine speech
Natural phenomena serve as vessels for spiritual influence from the higher worlds
